jobs.description:
Take high-performance and low-latency development to the next level with CGI  
  
Are you an experienced C++ / C# developer who thrives on solving complex challenges involving real-time systems, low latency, multithreading, parallel computing and distributed architectures?  
CGI is looking for a C# / C++ Developer – Real-Time Systems Expert to help design, optimize and modernize mission-critical technology platforms supporting pricing, risk calculation and financial markets activities within a major banking environment.  
You will work in a technology ecosystem where performance, scalability, resilience and speed matter. These platforms process significant volumes of data and transactions every day while supporting a broad range of users, including Front Office teams, quantitative risk analysts and risk managers.  
Your challenge: build and optimize systems capable of processing increasing volumes of transactions and calculations while meeting demanding performance and regulatory requirements.  
  
Work model: Hybrid – 3 days in the office after the first 2 months  
Location: Montréal

**Your future duties and responsibilities**

As a senior C++ / C# expert, you will play a key role in the evolution and modernization of critical real-time and distributed computing platforms.  
Your responsibilities will include:  

* Design, develop and enhance high-performance services using C++, C# and .NET Core.
* Develop and optimize real-time and low-latency C++ components.
* Design and optimize parallel algorithms for multicore architectures.
* Improve the performance and scalability of multithreaded applications.
* Contribute to the architecture and evolution of high-performance distributed systems.
* Perform profiling, monitoring, troubleshooting and performance optimization.
* Investigate complex performance issues and provide production support for mission-critical systems.
* Help redesign and modernize the real-time infrastructure and grid-oriented components.
* Contribute to the migration and evolution of computing workloads toward ArmoniK and cloud-based architectures.
* Participate in cloud bursting, cloud-native and Kubernetes initiatives.
* Collaborate closely with Front Office teams, quantitative analysts, risk teams and technology specialists.
* Contribute to the technology roadmap and architectural governance.
* Promote software engineering best practices related to code quality, performance, observability, scalability and resilience.

**Required qualifications to be successful in this role**

What we’re looking for  
Must-have skills  

* Strong hands-on experience with C++ and C# / .NET Core development.
* Proven expertise in real-time and low-latency C++ software development.
* Strong knowledge of multithreading, concurrency and parallel programming.
* Experience designing and optimizing parallel algorithms for multicore architectures.
* Strong experience developing high-performance distributed systems.
* Proven expertise in profiling, monitoring and performance optimization.
* Experience supporting and troubleshooting complex, production-critical systems.
* Strong software design and development practices.
* Ability to work independently and take ownership of complex technical challenges.
* Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
* Strong interest in emerging technologies and modern software engineering practices.

Previous experience with electronic markets, pricing, market making, trading platforms or capital markets technology is highly desirable.  
  
Why join CGI?  
This opportunity is ideal for someone who wants to go beyond traditional application development and work on technology where every millisecond matters.  
You will tackle real-world challenges involving low latency, parallel computing, high-performance C++, distributed processing and massive scalability, while contributing to systems that directly support critical financial markets activities.  
You will also play a role in a major technology transformation combining C++, .NET, distributed computing, Kubernetes and cloud technologies, while collaborating with technology, quantitative and financial markets specialists.  
  
If you enjoy understanding where every millisecond goes and pushing systems to their performance limits, this could be your next challenge at CGI.  
  
Work model: Hybrid – 3 days in the office after the first 2 months  
Location: Montréal  
  

* Ability to communicate in English, both orally and in writing, is a requirement as the person in this position will need to collaborate regularly with colleagues and partners in Canada and the United States.

  
CGI is providing a reasonable estimate of the pay range for this role. The determination of this range includes factors such as skill set level, geographic market, experience and training, and licenses and certifications. Compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $60,000–$115,000. This role is an existing vacancy.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

* Participer au développement et à l’évolution de solutions d’affaires dont l’envergure et les impacts sont majeurs pour l’entreprise.

The Train Control and Monitoring System (TCMS) team is involved in the improvement and troubleshooting of our customers active train fleets. The typical projects span from issue troubleshooting, obsolescence management to functional improvements.

The TCMS has an onboard and a wayside application: The onboard portion acquires train data, apply control rules and activates outputs for train operation. It also gathers multiple train health metrics that are sent to the wayside software over wireless links. The wayside application receives, processes, archives and makes this data available for consultation. This data is used for efficient train operation, preventive and reactive maintenance.

The team needs to increase its capacity into a distributed system with multi Operating Systems and programming languages environment, articulated through Network protocols, to fulfil our customers projects.

* Analyse data to define and validate technical solutions.
* Implement software solutions corresponding to client requirements.
* Troubleshoot, debug and assess onboard existing issues.

Every day, something extraordinary happens in the skies above Nunavik. At Air Inuit, we’re not just flying planes, we’re connecting communities, delivering essentials, and making a meaningful impact. Air Inuit’s aircraft have soared through some of the world’s most challenging skies, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

Reporting to the Finance team, the Cost and Route Profitability Analyst is responsible for developing a detailed understanding of operating costs and network profitability. The incumbent transforms financial and operational data into reliable analyses to assess the performance of routes, aircraft types, and the Passenger, Cargo, and Charter business segments, and provides recommendations to support decision-making.

At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, more than 80 000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars.

  

Alstom is experiencing unprecedented growth in Canada. To meet the challenges of tomorrow's transportation, we are looking for talents ready to combine global expertise with local impact.

  

Are you passionate about the railway world and complex systems? The Train Control & Monitoring Systems (TCMS) team opens its doors to you (**St-Bruno office, QC**).

The Train Control and Monitoring System (TCMS) team is involved in the improvement and troubleshooting of our customers active train fleets. The typical projects span from issue troubleshooting, obsolescence management to functional improvements.

The TCMS has an onboard and a wayside application: The onboard portion acquires train data, apply control rules and activates outputs for train operation. It also gathers multiple train health metrics that are sent to the wayside software over wireless links. The wayside application receives, processes, archives and makes this data available for consultation. This data is used for efficient train operation, preventive and reactive maintenance.

The team needs to increase its capacity into a distributed system with multi Operating Systems and programming languages environment, articulated through Network protocols, to fulfil our customers projects.

**Key Responsibilities**

As an **onboard Software developer**, you will be responsible for the maintenance and improvement of the various software components as well as being a key player in the related design and troubleshooting of train software and build process tools.

The Software developer works in close relationship with the Software Testers and System Engineers towards the delivery of a reliable and issue free software in compliance with established processes in a continuous build, integration and delivery fashion.

  

You are responsible to:

* Analyse data to define and validate technical solutions.
* Implement software solutions corresponding to client requirements.
* Troubleshoot, debug and assess onboard existing issues.
* Maintain and improve software development ecosystem (coding, configuration management, continuous integration, test tools, etc…)
* Participate in the entire software development lifecycle (analysis, design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance).
* Write technical reports that comply with company standards.

  

**Your profile**

You will have a demonstrable knowledge and capability across a range of different computer operating systems, medium-high software programming and network knowledge.

Candidate must be versatile, resourceful, autonomous and handy at intervening on existing SW components.

  

**Profile & Technical Skills**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical/Electronic Engineering, or equivalent.
* **3–5 years** of experience in embedded software development.
* Strong programming skills in **C, C++, C#**.
* Good knowledge of scripting/programming languages such as **Python, Bash/Shell scripting, and PowerShell**.
* Experience with **RTOS and** **embedded Linux**.
* Comfortable working in both **Windows** and **Linux** development environments.
* Good understanding of **embedded systems**, **multithreading**, **memory management**, **inter-process communication**, and r**eal-time constraints**.
* Knowledge of communication protocols and interfaces such as **Ethernet, TCP/IP, UDP, CAN, UART, SPI, and I²C**.
* Experience with **Git** or any other source control, **branching**, and **code review** practices.
* Familiarity with build systems and toolchains such as **CMake**, **Make**, **GCC**, and **cross-compilation**.
* Experience with **debugging** (analyzing engineering log, Wireshark, etc), **unit testing**, and **integration testing**.
* Familiarity with **CI/CD** (Git piplines, jenkin jobs, …) and automated build/test environments.
* Knowledge of **object-oriented programming**, **software architecture**, and design principles.
* Ability to analyze **software requirements** and produce clear technical documentation.
* Good analytical, troubleshooting, problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.

  

**What you will enjoy in this role and working at ALSTOM**

* Working daily in an innovative project environment
* Receiving a competitive salary including full social coverage (life, health, retirement) from the start of employment
* Developing new skills and your full potential through the continuous training offered

Alstom connaît une croissance sans précédent au Canada. Pour répondre aux défis du transport de demain, nous recherchons des talents prêts à conjuguer expertise mondiale et impact local.  
  
Vous êtes passionné par l'univers ferroviaire et les systèmes complexes ? L’équipe Train Control & Monitoring Systems (TCMS) vous ouvre ses portes (bureau **St-Bruno, Qc**).

L’équipe **TCMS (Système de contrôle et de surveillance des trains)** est responsable

de l’amélioration et du diagnostic des flottes de trains en service chez nos clients. Les projets typiques couvrent un large éventail d’activités, allant de la résolution de problèmes, la gestion de l’obsolescence jusqu’à l’amélioration fonctionnelle des systèmes.

Le TCMS est composé d’une application embarquée et d’une application au sol. La partie embarquée acquiert les données du train, applique les règles de contrôle et active les sorties nécessaires au fonctionnement du train. Elle collecte également de nombreux indicateurs relatifs à l’état de santé du train, qui sont transmis au logiciel sol par l’intermédiaire de liaisons sans fil.
